erces_triggers.code: 2022 NYC Building Code (as amended by Local Law 77 of 2023)
erces_triggers.rule: An ARCS (Auxiliary Radio Communication System) is required in high-rise buildings built under BC 403, underground buildings built under BC 405, and buildings with a total gross area over 250,000 sq ft. Exceptions: Group R-2 buildings whose highest occupied floor is under 125 ft above the lowest FDNY vehicle access, with no more than 1 story below grade and no more than 250,000 sq ft; or where FDNY decides a system is not needed. BC 916.1.1: construction documents go to FDNY for approval before installation.
erces_triggers.threshold: High-rise (FDNY bulletin: generally buildings over 75 ft); underground building; or gross area over 250,000 sq ft. R-2 exemption below 125 ft / 1 story below grade / 250,000 sq ft.

erces_triggers.code: 2022 NYC Building Code
erces_triggers.rule: Fire protection systems must be tested under the Building Code and Fire Code. It is unlawful to occupy any portion of a structure until the required fire protection systems in that portion have been tested and approved. ARCS is a Chapter 9 fire protection system, so a required ARCS has to pass before that portion is occupied.
erces_triggers.threshold: Applies wherever BC 916.3 requires ARCS.

erces_triggers.code: FDNY Bureau of Fire Prevention Bulletin 2022-01 Revision 1 (issued Oct 24, 2022)
erces_triggers.section: Sections III and IV (relates to 2014 BC 907.2.13.2 and 2022 BC 916.3)
erces_triggers.rule: Says that generally all buildings over 75 ft, whatever the occupancy, have needed ARCS since the 2014 Building Code. New and existing buildings are exempt if all of these hold: Group R-1, R-2 or B; highest roof 150 ft or less above the lowest FDNY vehicle access; no more than one story below grade; total area 250,000 sq ft or less. An existing building that does not meet those can ask for a waiver only after a final Certificate of Occupancy and a fire alarm Letter of Approval are issued, with a DAQ commissioning test witnessed by a PE and an FDNY DAQ acceptance test.
erces_triggers.threshold: Exempt: R-1/R-2/B, roof 150 ft or less, 1 story below grade or less, 250,000 sq ft or less. Anything taller, deeper, larger or of another occupancy needs ARCS or a waiver.

erces_triggers.code: FDNY ARCS Plan Submission and Approval Procedures (Rev 7/11/2024); FDNY rule 3 RCNY 510-01 (formerly 511-01)
erces_triggers.rule: The ARCS application needs a copy of the DOB Certificate of Occupancy or approved Schedule A for the whole building. After installation, an ARC System Professional (Certificate of Fitness holder) runs a commissioning test. FDNY accepts the report, then the FDNY Fire Alarm Inspection Unit runs an inspection and acceptance test, and FDNY issues a Letter of Approval for the system. Recertification test every 5 years. Application fee on the NYC Business page: $585 new.
erces_triggers.threshold: None beyond BC 916.3.

erces_triggers.ahj: New York City (FDNY / NYC Business portal)
erces_triggers.code: NYC Business, Auxiliary Radio Communication System Application page
erces_triggers.rule: Says the 2014 Building Code requires ARCS in newly built high-rise buildings and in existing buildings that have gone through major changes. The page does not define major changes. Note: in the 2022 code, BC 403.4.4 is the emergency voice/alarm section; the ARCS requirement moved to BC 916.3 (FC 511 and BC 917 in older citations are now FC 510 and BC 916).
erces_triggers.threshold: Existing buildings with major changes; no area or percentage given.

erces_triggers.code: 2023 City of Los Angeles Fire Code (LAMC Ch. 5 Art. 7, based on 2022 CFC), UpCodes copy
erces_triggers.rule: Two-way emergency responder coverage is required in all new buildings, measured against the outdoor signal. Exceptions: a wired system approved by both officials, the fire code official decides it is not needed, or an automatically activated system where a live one would disrupt the facility. Existing buildings go to Chapter 11: 1103.2 requires coverage where an existing wired system cannot be repaired or is being replaced, or within a time frame the adopting authority sets. A construction permit is required to install or modify a system. The LA text read shows no LA amendment to 510 and no alteration threshold.
erces_triggers.threshold: None in the code text read.

erces_triggers.code: LAFD enforcement language reported by BOMA (trade article, Mar 21, 2022)
erces_triggers.rule: The article says that from Aug 7, 2018, LAFD requires an ERRCS where a building has more than three stories above grade plane, 50,000 sq ft or more total area, 10,000 sq ft or more of basement, or any basement level two or more stories below grade. It says new developments have been refused a certificate of occupancy for lacking a system. No LAFD document, number or URL is given. No LAFD page with these thresholds was found (lafd.org search empty; ICC LA Fire Code and amlegal LAMC 57.510 pages returned 403). No LAFD alteration threshold (percent or square feet) was found anywhere.
erces_triggers.threshold: More than 3 stories; 50,000 sq ft or more; basement 10,000 sq ft or more; 2 or more levels below grade (trade source only).

erces_triggers.ahj: Los Angeles County Fire Department (unincorporated county and contract cities, not the City of LA)
erces_triggers.code: LACoFD Inspection Guideline V7-C3-S21, Emergency Responder Radio Coverage (02/02/2023)
erces_triggers.section: IV.A.1 Evaluation of need; plan note 17.a; IV.D Acceptance test
erces_triggers.rule: Buildings or portions that are new, or that otherwise trigger the current code (for example a change of occupancy classification or use), must be evaluated for ERRCS if they have two or more stories above grade, any level below grade, or 10,000 sq ft or more total area, or if the fire code official says so. One- and two-family homes and townhouses are exempt. The ERRCS may not be powered on before the fire code official's final inspection (except into a non-radiating load). The final acceptance test is run by the fire code official and is not complete until as-built plans are received.
erces_triggers.threshold: 2 or more stories; any below-grade level; 10,000 sq ft or more. Change of occupancy or use triggers evaluation.

erces_triggers.code: SFFD Administrative Bulletin 2.01 (2025), Addendum G; 2025 SFFC 510.1, 510.1.1, 1103.2, CFC 1103.7.9.8
erces_triggers.rule: New low-rise buildings: when construction is complete, a coverage test is run; if it fails, an ERCES must be installed. New high-rise buildings: an ERCES is always required, and a wired phone-jack system is not allowed instead. Existing buildings that need a building permit for a change of occupancy must have coverage and a coverage test, unless they have a working phone-jack system. Existing high-rises with no phone-jack system must run a coverage test; if it fails, an ERCES must be installed within 3 years of the test date. Exception for one-story buildings up to 12,000 sq ft with no basement. Passing tests are recorded on the fire alarm permit plans or on a separate permit and checked at an inspection after the SF Department of Technology signs off.
erces_triggers.threshold: Exempt: one story, 12,000 sq ft or less, no basement. Change-of-occupancy permit triggers it. Existing high-rise: 3 years after a failed test.

erces_triggers.code: 2025 San Francisco Fire Code; SFFD Administrative Bulletin 3.04 (2025)
erces_triggers.section: SFFC 510.6.1.1, 510.6.1.2; AB 3.04 sections I and II
erces_triggers.rule: All new ERCES must be certificated by an OSHA NRTL organization, with the certificate at the BDA annunciator. Owners of all existing ERCES must also get a certificate (effective 1/1/2023 per AB 2.01). Every ERCES contractor needs the certification, and a copy goes on every ERCES permit plan set. From 1/1/2023 all new ERCES equipment must be UL 2524 listed.
erces_triggers.threshold: All ERCES, new and existing.

erces_triggers.code: Chicago Building Code (Title 14B, 2019, based on 2018 IBC)
erces_triggers.rule: Chicago did not adopt IBC Section 918 (Emergency Responder Radio Coverage): '14B-9-918 The provisions of Section 918 of IBC are not adopted' (Coun. J. 4-10-19). High-rises instead get a wired two-way fire department communication system between the fire command center and stations at least every fifth level and in exit stairs (907.2.12.2.1). The building code has no radio-coverage trigger. The Chicago Fire Prevention Code was not found online and was not checked.
erces_triggers.threshold: None for radio coverage in the building code.

erces_triggers.code: 2021 Seattle Fire Code
erces_triggers.rule: An ERCES is required in new buildings that are high-rise, or 50,000 sq ft or more total, or have 10,000 sq ft or more of basement, or have occupied floors more than 30 ft below the lowest exit discharge. Install to 510.4 to 510.5.8 and NFPA 1225 (2022). Exception: buildings or areas that already meet PSERN signal levels inside without an ERCES.
erces_triggers.threshold: High-rise; 50,000 sq ft or more; basement 10,000 sq ft or more; occupied floor more than 30 ft below exit discharge.

erces_triggers.code: 2021 Seattle Fire Code
erces_triggers.rule: After the acceptance test and before the building certificate of occupancy is issued, the owner must put the certification letter, grid diagrams, equipment data, wiring diagram and electrical permit in the DAS enclosure or engineer's office, and must submit the acceptance test report to the fire code official through thecomplianceengine.com.
erces_triggers.threshold: Every building where 510.1 requires ERCES.

erces_triggers.code: 2021 Seattle Fire Code
erces_triggers.rule: Existing high-rise buildings must provide coverage under Section 510. Buildings built under a code earlier than the 2015 Seattle Fire Code are exempt if they have a wired communication system under 907.2.12.2 or already have acceptable signal strength under 510.4.1. Seattle struck the model 1103.2 triggers (wired system not repairable, or a local time frame). The 2021 text has no substantial-alteration trigger for ERCES; 'substantial alteration' appears only in 507.1 (water supply).
erces_triggers.threshold: Existing high-rise only.

erces_triggers.code: 2025 Denver Fire Code (amendments to 2024 IFC)
erces_triggers.rule: ERCES coverage is required in high-rise buildings, underground buildings, and airport buildings. Other new buildings must be tested at substantial completion if they are: Type I or II over 50,000 gross sq ft; Group E or I with over 12,000 gross sq ft on any story; Type III, IV or V over 100,000 gross sq ft with masonry shafts, walls or floors; or have over 10,000 gross sq ft of occupiable below-ground area. If coverage fails, an ERCES is required. Buildings that pass are retested every 5 years under DFD Policy 510-1.
erces_triggers.threshold: Type I/II over 50,000 gsf; E/I over 12,000 gsf on a story; Type III/IV/V over 100,000 gsf with masonry; below-ground over 10,000 gsf.

erces_triggers.code: 2025 Denver Fire Code (amendments to 2024 IFC)
erces_triggers.rule: Existing high-rise, underground, I-1, I-2, I-3, E and airport buildings must be tested for radio coverage when they install a Mass Notification System or replace the complete fire alarm head-end. If coverage is deficient, an ERCES is required. Buildings that pass are retested every 5 years.
erces_triggers.threshold: Triggered by an MNS install or a full fire alarm head-end replacement (a fire alarm permit), not by floor area.

erces_triggers.code: 2025 Denver Fire Code (amendments to 2024 IFC)
erces_triggers.rule: A construction permit is required to install or modify an ERCES, including maintenance. Shop drawings with RF grids are a deferred submittal and must be approved before installation. An operational permit is required for the annual and 5-year tests.
erces_triggers.threshold: All ERCES.

erces_triggers.code: Phoenix Fire Code 2024 (2024 IFC with amendments; UpCodes shows effective Feb 17, 2026)
erces_triggers.rule: An ERCES is required in all new buildings; the 2024 IFC exceptions include one-story buildings up to 12,000 sq ft with no below-ground area. Phoenix 510.1.1: new buildings that pass a benchmark test need no annual retest, but must retest on new construction or a tenant improvement, a change of occupancy or use, a flag from operations or other public safety departments, or when the fire code official requires it. Permits are required for modifications, including frequency list changes, BDA replacement, donor antenna changes and re-optimization with the Regional Wireless Cooperative.
erces_triggers.threshold: Retest on any tenant improvement or change of occupancy/use (no area threshold).

erces_triggers.code: Phoenix Fire Prevention Explanatory Policy, Emergency Responder Radio Coverage (effective Dec 2021, reviewed July 2024; cites 2018 PFC 510 and 1103.2, NFPA 1225-2022)
erces_triggers.section: Scope; Testing and Compliance Procedure; Certificate of Radio Coverage Compliance
erces_triggers.rule: Applies to new and existing buildings with more than three stories above grade, over 50,000 sq ft total, any basement or underground level, or where the fire code official requires it and signal is below PFC 510 levels. Test after the building envelope is complete (doors, windows, interior walls). Before the building Certificate of Occupancy, a Certificate of Radio Coverage Compliance sealed by an Arizona PE must be submitted; a TCO may be issued case by case. Annual testing; reports go to The Compliance Engine. The policy cites the 2018 PFC, while Phoenix now runs the 2024 PFC.
erces_triggers.threshold: More than 3 stories; over 50,000 sq ft; any basement.

erces_triggers.code: 2024 IFC with Austin local amendments (City Code 25-12, effective July 10, 2025)
erces_triggers.section: 510.1, 1103.2 (model text); 510.5.3 is the only Section 510 amendment in the ordinance draft read
erces_triggers.rule: Austin runs the model 2024 IFC 510.1: an ERCES is required in all new buildings, with the 2024 exceptions, including one-story buildings up to 12,000 sq ft with no below-ground area. Existing buildings follow model 1103.2: required where a wired system cannot be repaired or is being replaced, or within a time frame the adopting authority sets. No Austin time frame or alteration threshold was found; the 2021 cycle had removed Austin's earlier 510.1.1 and 510.1.2 time-frame amendments. The section list was read in the 3/28/2025 Law Dept draft (Council file 25-0615, Apr 10, 2025), not the final signed ordinance.
erces_triggers.threshold: None found beyond the model code.

erces_triggers.code: 2021 Houston Fire Code (UpCodes copy)
erces_triggers.rule: New buildings need compliance verification testing by a City of Houston registered ERCC third-party special inspector. The report must go to the building official before the project's final approval or the Certificate of Occupancy. Exception: buildings with no basement, three stories or less, and 50,000 sq ft or less total.
erces_triggers.threshold: Exempt: no basement, 3 stories or less, 50,000 sq ft or less.

erces_triggers.code: 2021 Houston Fire Code (UpCodes copy)
erces_triggers.rule: Alterations to existing buildings need compliance verification testing by a City of Houston registered ERCC third-party special inspector. The report must go to the building official before the project's final approval or the Certificate of Compliance or Certificate of Occupancy. Same exemption as new buildings (no basement, 3 stories or less, 50,000 sq ft or less).
erces_triggers.threshold: Any alteration permit in a building that has a basement, more than 3 stories, or more than 50,000 sq ft. No percentage or area threshold for the alteration itself.

erces_triggers.code: 2021 Houston Fire Code (UpCodes copy)
erces_triggers.rule: Existing buildings other than R-3 that lack coverage must add it where a wired system cannot be repaired or is being replaced. Where an existing building is found in violation of Section 510, the owner must fix it and file for building permits within a time frame the fire code official sets.
erces_triggers.threshold: None.

erces_triggers.code: Form CE-1350, Building Code Enforcement ERRC Guideline (revised Nov 16, 2022)
erces_triggers.section: Purpose; Existing Facilities; New Construction; Parts 2 to 4
erces_triggers.rule: From June 6, 2018, the code analysis sheet on all new-building plans and all remodel and lease buildout plans must state ERRC compliance (Houston BC 914, FC 510). New construction gets a pretest; before the CO or final inspection, a registered third-party ERRC special inspector tests and the report goes to HPC-RA@houstontx.gov. ERRC plans may be a deferred submittal (Form CE-1086). Installing or replacing ERRC equipment is a building permit with the fee based on construction cost. Plan review and special inspection are exempt for buildings with no basement, 3 stories or less, and 50,000 sq ft or less. The text was read from a vendor-hosted copy; the city's own site returned 403, and the city says CE-1350 was later updated for the 2021 codes.
erces_triggers.threshold: Exempt: no basement, 3 stories or less, 50,000 sq ft or less.

erces_triggers.code: 2024 International Fire Code
erces_triggers.rule: "Approved in-building emergency responder communications enhancement system (ERCES) for emergency responders shall be provided in all new buildings", based on existing coverage of the public safety system measured at the exterior of the building. Exceptions: 1. a wired system per 907.2.13.2 where both the building official and fire code official approve; 2. where the fire code official decides the system is not needed; 3. an automatically activated system where a live one could hurt normal operations; 4. "One-story buildings not exceeding 12,000 square feet (1115 m2) with no below-ground area(s)." 510.3.1: a construction permit is required to install or modify an ERCES (105.6.5); 510.3.2: an operational permit where the fire code official requires one.
erces_triggers.threshold: All new buildings, except one-story buildings of 12,000 sq ft or less with no below-ground area. No height or occupancy gate.

erces_triggers.code: 2024 International Fire Code
erces_triggers.rule: "Where an in-building emergency responder communications enhancement system is required, and upon completion of installation, the building owner shall have the radio system tested to verify that two-way coverage on each floor of the building is not less than 95 percent." Grid of 20 test areas per floor; failure of more than one area fails the test. The model text ties the test to completion of installation, not expressly to the certificate of occupancy; local codes often add the CO tie.
erces_triggers.threshold: Every building where 510.1 requires an ERCES.

erces_triggers.code: 2024 International Fire Code
erces_triggers.rule: The owner "shall have the in-building emergency responder communications enhancement system inspected and tested annually or where structural changes occur, including additions or remodels that could materially change the original field performance tests." Retest = full in-building coverage test (510.5.4), booster gain check, 1-hour battery load test, report to the fire code official.
erces_triggers.threshold: Any addition or remodel that could materially change the original field test results. No area, value or percentage threshold.

erces_triggers.code: 2024 International Fire Code
erces_triggers.rule: Existing buildings other than Group R-3 without approved ERCES shall be equipped "according to one of the following: 1. Where an existing wired communication system cannot be repaired or is being replaced, or where not approved in accordance with Section 510.1, Exception 1. 2. Within a time frame established by the adopting authority." Exception: fire code official decides it is not needed. Table 1103.1 marks 1103.2 required for high-rise, atrium/covered mall, underground buildings and Groups A, B, E, F, H, I, M, R-1, R-2, S; not R-3, R-4 or tire storage.
erces_triggers.threshold: Existing building (not R-3/R-4) whose wired firefighter phone system fails or is being replaced, or a local retrofit deadline.

erces_triggers.code: 2021 International Fire Code
erces_triggers.rule: "Approved in-building, two-way emergency responder communication coverage for emergency responders shall be provided in all new buildings." Same three exceptions as 2018 (approved wired system per 907.2.13.2; fire code official decides not needed; automatically activated system). No size exemption. 510.3: construction permit to install or modify (105.6.4).
erces_triggers.threshold: All new buildings; no building-size exemption in this edition.

erces_triggers.code: 2021 International Fire Code
erces_triggers.rule: Annual test "or where structural changes occur, including additions or remodels that could materially change the original field performance tests."
erces_triggers.threshold: Additions or remodels that could materially change the original field test. No numeric threshold.

erces_triggers.code: 2021 International Fire Code
erces_triggers.rule: Existing buildings other than Group R-3 without approved two-way coverage shall be equipped where an existing wired system cannot be repaired or is being replaced (or was not approved under 510.1 Exception 1), or within a time frame set by the adopting authority. Exception: fire code official decides not needed.
erces_triggers.threshold: Existing building (not R-3) with a failed or replaced wired system, or a local deadline.

erces_triggers.code: 2018 International Fire Code
erces_triggers.rule: "New buildings shall have approved radio coverage for emergency responders within the building based on the existing coverage levels of the public safety communication systems utilized by the jurisdiction, measured at the exterior of the building." Exceptions: wired system per 907.2.12.2 where both officials approve; fire code official decides not needed; automatically activated system. 510.3: construction permit to install or modify (105.7.6).
erces_triggers.threshold: All new buildings; no size exemption.

erces_triggers.code: 2018 International Fire Code
erces_triggers.rule: System "shall be inspected and tested annually or where structural changes occur including additions or remodels that could materially change the original field performance tests."
erces_triggers.threshold: Additions or remodels that could materially change the original field test. No numeric threshold.

erces_triggers.code: 2018 International Fire Code
erces_triggers.rule: Existing buildings other than Group R-3 without approved radio coverage shall be equipped where an existing wired system cannot be repaired or is being replaced (or was not approved under 510.1 Exception 1), or within a time frame set by the adopting authority. Exception: fire code official decides not needed.
erces_triggers.threshold: Existing building (not R-3) with a failed or replaced wired system, or a local deadline.

erces_triggers.code: 2024 International Building Code
erces_triggers.rule: "In-building two-way emergency responder communication coverage shall be provided in all new buildings in accordance with Section 510 of the International Fire Code." The building code points to IFC 510, so the requirement is reviewed at building permit plan review.
erces_triggers.threshold: All new buildings, with the IFC 510.1 exceptions.

erces_triggers.code: 2018 International Building Code
erces_triggers.rule: "Emergency responder radio coverage shall be provided in all new buildings in accordance with Section 510 of the International Fire Code."
erces_triggers.threshold: All new buildings, with the IFC 510.1 exceptions.

erces_triggers.code: 2021 Virginia Construction Code (USBC Part I, 2021 IBC amended; effective Jan 18, 2024)
erces_triggers.rule: "For localities utilizing public safety wireless communications, dedicated infrastructure to accommodate and perpetuate continuous in-building emergency communication equipment ... shall be provided in new buildings and structures." Exceptions: 1. Use Groups A-5, I-4, within dwelling units of R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, and U; 2. Types IV and V construction without basements that are not unlimited area buildings (Section 507); 3. "Above grade single story buildings of less than 20,000 square feet"; 4. government or contractor buildings with security requirements and an approved alternative; 5. owner provides documentation from a qualified individual that the structure does not impede signals; 6. buildings in localities that do not provide the additional equipment needed to run the system.
erces_triggers.threshold: New buildings in localities that use public safety wireless radio. Exempt: single-story above grade under 20,000 sq ft; Type IV/V without basement (not unlimited area); A-5, I-4, U; inside R-2 to R-5 dwelling units.

erces_triggers.code: 2021 Virginia Construction Code
erces_triggers.rule: 918.1.1: systems comply with IFC 510.4 and 510.5, "except that the acceptance testing procedure required by Section 510.5.4 of the International Fire Code shall be the responsibility of the locality." The owner installs cabling in dedicated conduits/raceways; the locality installs any additional equipment and (918.1.2) operates and maintains it. 918.1.3: inspected before concealment. 918.2: "Upon completion of installation" emergency public safety personnel may enter to field-test coverage "at no cost to the owner" and report deficiencies to the owner.
erces_triggers.threshold: Every building where 918.1 applies.

erces_triggers.code: 2021 Virginia Statewide Fire Prevention Code (2021 IFC amended)
erces_triggers.rule: Section 510 is retitled maintenance of in-building emergency communication equipment. 510.2: "If it is determined by the locality that increased amplification of their emergency communication system is needed, the building owner shall allow the locality access as well as provide appropriate space within the building to install and maintain necessary additional communication equipment by the locality. If the building owner denies the locality access or appropriate space, or both, the building owner shall be responsible for the installation and maintenance of these additional systems." 510.3: fire official or police chief may field-test at no cost to the owner. 510.4, 510.5 and 510.6 (including the 510.6.1 retest) are deleted, and SFPC Chapter 11 (1103.2) is deleted in its entirety.
erces_triggers.threshold: Existing buildings where the locality decides more amplification is needed. No size threshold.

erces_triggers.code: 2021 Virginia Existing Building Code
erces_triggers.rule: 801.1: "Additions to any building or structure shall comply with the requirements of the Virginia Construction Code (VCC) for new construction"; a fire wall per VCC 706 makes the addition a separate building. 803.1: "Additions to existing buildings or structures are new construction." 802.3: "Existing fire areas increased by the addition shall comply with Chapter 9 of the VCC" (VCC 918 is in Chapter 9). So VCC 918.1 reaches the addition, and the enlarged fire area, when the addition's own size and type fall outside the 918 exceptions.
erces_triggers.threshold: Any addition; the 918.1 exceptions (for example single-story under 20,000 sq ft) are applied to the addition or enlarged fire area.

erces_triggers.code: Arlington County Code Ch. 8.1, Fire Prevention Code (updated April 2025), amending the SFPC
erces_triggers.rule: Adds 510.2.1 Internal antenna/amplifier systems: "As determined by the fire code official, or as otherwise required by Arlington County, increased amplification systems are required in certain structures and construction features." Systems must meet the IFC in-building emergency communications coverage standards; "Where required or installed, building owners shall provide sufficient space and conduit for the systems and access to permit installation, testing, inspection and maintenance by the county or, as otherwise required, by the building owner." The fee table lists the bi-directional antenna system under 510.2.1 and "Zoning-Site Condition # 37", inspected every 6 months ($200), which points to a site plan approval condition as a second source of the requirement.
erces_triggers.threshold: Case by case (fire code official or County, including site plan conditions). No size threshold in the text.

erces_triggers.code: Fairfax County Office of the Fire Marshal, ERCES Submittal and Permit Requirements Guidelines, Version 2, September 2025 (applies VCC 2021 918, IFC 2021, NFPA 1225 2022)
erces_triggers.section: Introduction; Steps 1-5; Code Modification Process for High-Rise Projects
erces_triggers.rule: The owner reviews VCC 918 to decide if a system is required; steps apply to any required or voluntary ERCES. Step 1: DIT Radio Services design approval and Retransmission Authorization. Step 2: LDS building permit required for "New construction" and "If there are any penetrations through fire-rated assemblies in existing buildings." Step 3: Electrical/Low Voltage Voice/Data permit (building permit first for new construction). Step 4: full ERCES needs a fire alarm system permit. Step 5: an In-Building Emergency Communications Coverage (FCOMM) permit "is required for all system installations" with a signed maintenance agreement. High-rise: firefighter phones remain required by VCC; installing ERCES in lieu of them needs a code modification (CDMOD).
erces_triggers.threshold: New construction (VCC 918.1 exceptions apply); existing-building installs need a building permit only when they penetrate fire-rated assemblies.

erces_triggers.code: Fairfax County ERCES Submittal and Permit Requirements Guidelines, Version 2, September 2025
erces_triggers.rule: "System inspection and acceptance testing will be performed by DIT, LDS, and OFM." DIT Radio Services inspects and tests first; after DIT approval the fire alarm, building and emergency communications coverage inspections proceed (LDS trade inspectors; OFM acceptance testing inspectors). The guideline does not name the certificate of occupancy; these are final inspections on the permits listed above.
erces_triggers.threshold: Every FCOMM permit.

erces_triggers.code: 2017 DC Fire Code (12-H DCMR, 2015 IFC amended; effective May 29, 2020), UpCodes copy
erces_triggers.rule: "All new buildings shall have approved radio coverage for emergency responders within the building based upon the existing coverage levels of the public safety communication systems of the District of Columbia at the exterior of the building." Exceptions: approved wired system per 907.2.13.2; where the DC Office of Unified Communications (OUC) and the fire code official decide it is not needed under OUC guidelines; automatically activated system; "Building covered by the Residential Code"; "Group R-2 buildings with four or fewer dwelling units per floor up to three floors above grade"; "Group R-3 buildings." 510.3: no system may be installed or modified "without a building permit and any required electrical permit issued by the building code official." 510.7: systems must meet all OUC requirements.
erces_triggers.threshold: All new buildings except IRC buildings, R-3, and R-2 with 4 or fewer units per floor and up to 3 floors above grade.

erces_triggers.code: 2017 DC Fire Code (12-H DCMR), UpCodes copy
erces_triggers.rule: Existing buildings without approved radio coverage "shall be equipped with such coverage in accordance with Section 510, within the time frame established by the District of Columbia Office of Unified Communications (OUC) and the fire code official in the following cases: Where no communication system is installed and operational; Where an existing wired communication system cannot be repaired; Where an existing wired communication system is being replaced; or Where an existing wired communication system was not approved in accordance with Section 510.1, Exception 1." Exception: OUC and fire code official decide not needed. Table 1103.1 in the DC text marks 1103.2 required for every listed use and occupancy, R-3 included.
erces_triggers.threshold: Any existing building with no working communication system (radio or wired), or a failed or replaced wired system; timing set by OUC and the fire code official.

erces_triggers.code: 2017 DC Fire Code (12-H DCMR), UpCodes copy
erces_triggers.rule: System "shall be inspected and tested annually or where structural changes occur including additions or remodels that could materially change the original field performance tests."
erces_triggers.threshold: Additions or remodels that could materially change the original field test.

erces_triggers.code: OUC, Public Safety In-Building Radio Systems Implementation and Operations Process, Version 3.1
erces_triggers.section: 2.2 to 2.4 and the retransmission authorization section
erces_triggers.rule: Owners apply for construction permits with DCRA (now DOB); after the building permit the owner applies to OUC for frequency retransmission and OUC must validate the design before construction of the DAS starts. For an existing building (not in construction), the design package must include RSSI measurements "that demonstrate that an in-building radio system is necessary." The OUC retransmission letter states that "when significant modifications will be made to the building affecting radio waves propagation and/or levels of interference, the building owner shall perform again a public safety BDA/DAS test at his cost using one of the OUC approved vendors"; listed examples: "adding interior/exterior walls, ceiling, partitions", "extending the Distributed Antennas System", "implementing additional wireless systems (internal systems or cellular systems for instance)". Extent of retest decided case by case.
erces_triggers.threshold: Any tenant fit-out or remodel that adds walls, ceilings or partitions in a building with an OUC-authorized system.

erces_triggers.code: COMAR 29.06.01 (NFPA 1 2024 and NFPA 101 2024 incorporated by reference; Reg .08 effective 6/23/2025)
erces_triggers.rule: Maryland adopts NFPA 1 (2024) and NFPA 101 (2024). Regulation .08 amends NFPA 1 9.15.1 and 9.15.2 "to insert the words 'and the AHJ' after 'NFPA 1225'" and lists no amendment to NFPA 1 Section 11.10 (in-building emergency responder communication enhancement systems) in the text read. So the NFPA 1 11.10 rule applies as published: minimum radio signal strength in new and existing buildings at a level the AHJ sets, with enhancement systems where required by the AHJ, per NFPA 1225. The NFPA 1 2024 base text itself was not read on NFPA's site (paywalled).
erces_triggers.threshold: AHJ-determined; no state size threshold. COMAR 29.06.01.03D: does not apply to dwellings for not more than two families; .03C: Baltimore City only as prescribed by statute.

erces_triggers.section: .05B(4) definition of New building or condition; .03A
erces_triggers.rule: "'New building or condition' means a building, structure, installation, plant, equipment, renovation, or condition: (a) For which a building permit is issued on or after the effective date of this chapter; ... (c) Which represents a change from one occupancy classification to another on or after the effective date of this chapter". .03A: the chapter applies to new and existing buildings; existing requirements may be modified where impractical in the AHJ's judgment. Effect: a renovation that pulls a building permit, or a change of occupancy classification, is held to new-building rules, including whatever NFPA 1 11.10 coverage level the AHJ sets.
erces_triggers.threshold: Any renovation with a building permit issued after the code's effective date; any change of occupancy classification.

erces_triggers.code: Executive Regulation 13-24 (COMCOR 08.00.02, 2021 IBC adoption), effective December 10, 2024
erces_triggers.rule: "Emergency responder radio coverage must be assured in the following areas of all newly constructed buildings: 1. below ground floors of a building, 2. all floors in buildings greater than 25,000 ft2 per floor, and 3. to all floors of buildings greater than 3 stories in height. One- and two-family dwellings and townhouses are exempt from this requirement." 918.2: floor areas that cannot reach the coverage level set by the County Department of Technology Services "must be provided with an in-building public safety radio enhancement system under the Montgomery County Fire Safety Code."
erces_triggers.threshold: New buildings: any below-ground floor; any building over 25,000 sq ft per floor; any building over 3 stories. Exempt: 1-2 family and townhouses.

erces_triggers.code: Executive Regulation 13-24 (COMCOR 08.00.02), effective December 10, 2024
erces_triggers.rule: "Emergency responder radio coverage and in-building public safety radio enhancement system must be tested[,] and inspected by approved individuals. The results of the testing and inspection must be certified to the code official before issuance of an occupancy permit."
erces_triggers.threshold: Every building covered by 918.1.

erces_triggers.code: Executive Regulation 14-24, Fire Safety Code - Building Construction (COMCOR 22.00.07), effective December 10, 2024
erces_triggers.rule: "For newly constructed buildings, ERRCES must be provided where any of the following conditions exist: (1) on all floors of a building located below the level of exit discharge; (2) on all floors of a building in which any floor of the building exceeds 25,000 ft2 per floor in gross aggregate area; (3) throughout any building in which the building area exceeds 100,000 ft2 in gross aggregate area; and (4) on all floors of a building for any building greater than three (3) stories in height above the lowest level of fire department vehicle access." "(b) Compliance testing must be performed at time of occupancy." Exception: one- and two-family dwellings and townhomes.
erces_triggers.threshold: New buildings: below exit discharge; any floor over 25,000 sq ft; total over 100,000 sq ft; over 3 stories above lowest fire department access.

erces_triggers.code: Executive Regulation 14-24 (COMCOR 22.00.07), effective December 10, 2024
erces_triggers.rule: "In existing buildings, where emergency radio communication system performance is reported to be inadequate, and the building meets the criteria of 9.15.1(a) through (d), the Director is permitted to require a technical analysis" certified by a Maryland PE with at least five years of ERRCES experience; "Where the analysis demonstrates unacceptable performance, an in-building public safety radio enhancement system must be provided." The summary also states that existing buildings or systems which are altered are subject to the regulation "to the extent required by the Maryland Building [Performance Standards]".
erces_triggers.threshold: Existing buildings meeting the 9.15.1 size/height criteria where coverage is reported inadequate.

erces_triggers.code: Executive Regulation 14-24 (COMCOR 22.00.07), effective December 10, 2024
erces_triggers.rule: Acceptance test on the Montgomery County control channel, each floor mapped in grids no larger than 25 ft by 25 ft, each grid DAQ 3.5 or better; at most two non-adjacent failed grids per floor. 11.3.9.1.4: "Acceptance test data of the system must be approved by the AHJ prior to final fire alarm system approval." 22.00.07.188: NFPA 1225 (2022) Chapter 18 adopted in its entirety.
erces_triggers.threshold: Every required or installed system.

erces_triggers.code: CB-047-2025 (2021 IBC adoption; enacted Oct 7, 2025, effective Dec 12, 2025), Sec. 4-106(e) amending IBC 101.4.5
erces_triggers.rule: "Whenever this Code makes reference to the International Fire Code, the requirements of the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) 1 and Subtitle 11 of the Prince George's County Code shall apply" (listed exceptions are power, solar, storage, dust, medical gas, labs and energy storage). erces_triggers.code: Minnesota Rules 7511.7900 subp. 5, 2020 Minnesota State Fire Code (2018 IFC base; IFC 510 deleted by 7511.0510)
erces_triggers.rule: "The provisions contained in this appendix are not mandatory unless specifically referenced in the local adopting ordinance." Exceptions: approved wired system per 907.2.12.2; fire code official decides not needed; automatically activated system; "4. Where it is determined to be unreasonably burdensome to implement an approved radio coverage system." P103: construction permit to install or modify.

erces_triggers.code: Minnesota Rules 7511.7900 subp. 5

Whenever an existing wired communication system cannot be repaired or is being replaced, or where not approved. 2. Within a time frame established by the adopting authority." Exception: fire code official decides not needed.
erces_triggers.threshold: Adopting jurisdictions only: failed or replaced wired system, or a local deadline.

erces_triggers.code: Minnesota Rules 7511.7900 subp. 5
erces_triggers.rule: Where adopted: "inspected and tested annually or whenever structural changes occur including additions or remodels that could materially change the original field performance tests."
erces_triggers.threshold: Adopting jurisdictions only: additions or remodels that could materially change the original test.

erces_triggers.code: Bloomington City Code § 6.02 (Ord. 2023-6, passed 3-20-2023), American Legal copy
erces_triggers.rule: Bloomington adopts the Minnesota State Fire Code with "(1) Appendix I: Fire Protection Systems - Noncompliant Conditions; and (2) Appendix P: Emergency Responder Radio Coverage." erces_triggers.threshold: All new buildings (Appendix P P102 exceptions); existing per P101.

erces_triggers.code: 2018 North Carolina Fire Code (2015 IFC base), in force per the state. The 2024 code has no effective date yet
erces_triggers.rule: 510 requires approved in-building two-way emergency responder coverage in all new buildings, with exceptions. Exception 4: one-story buildings of 7,500 sq ft or less, not windowless, underground or with a basement. Corrected 11/5: the 12,000 sq ft figure is in the 2024 code, not the code in force.

erces_triggers.code: 2018 North Carolina Fire Code
erces_triggers.rule: Owner has the system "inspected and tested annually or where structural changes occur, including additions or remodels that could materially change the original field performance tests."
erces_triggers.threshold: Additions or remodels that could materially change the original field test.

erces_triggers.code: Session Law 2025-50 (House Bill 768), ratified June 25, 2025, approved July 2, 2025
erces_triggers.rule: "the following buildings and structures, whether existing, newly constructed, or altered after the effective date of this act, are exempt from those requirements: (1) R-2 Apartment Buildings of Type V construction that meet the egress requirements of the Code. erces_triggers.code: 2021 South Carolina Fire Code (2021 IFC with SC modifications; in force until the 2024 code on Jan 1, 2027), UpCodes copy

Three exceptions (wired system; fire code official decides not needed; automatically activated). No size exemption in this edition.
erces_triggers.threshold: All new buildings; no size exemption until Jan 1, 2027.

erces_triggers.code: 2021 and 2024 South Carolina Fire Code, UpCodes copy
erces_triggers.rule: High-rise buildings: "In-building, two-way emergency responder communication coverage shall be provided in accordance with Section 510." Charleston's bulletin reads this as "All high-rise buildings shall be equipped with an Emergency Responder Radio System, regardless of signal strength from Public Radio System, per SCFC 914.3.6."

erces_triggers.code: 2024 South Carolina Fire Code (2024 IFC with SC modifications), implementation January 1, 2027, UpCodes copy
erces_triggers.rule: Model 2024 IFC 510.1 with Exception 4 "One-story buildings not exceeding 12,000 square feet (1115 m2) with no below-ground area(s)." 510.2: existing buildings as required in Chapter 11. 510.3.1 construction permit; 510.3.2 operational permit where required. The 2024 SC modification index (11/3/2025 V.1) lists no modification to IFC 510 or Chapter 11.
erces_triggers.threshold: From Jan 1, 2027: all new buildings except one-story, 12,000 sq ft or less, no below-ground area.

erces_triggers.code: 2024 South Carolina Fire Code, UpCodes copy
erces_triggers.rule: Model 2024 IFC 1103.2 unmodified: existing buildings other than R-3 without approved ERCES must be equipped where an existing wired system cannot be repaired or is being replaced (or was not approved), or within a time frame established by the adopting authority.
erces_triggers.threshold: Existing building with failed or replaced wired system, or a local deadline.

erces_triggers.code: Charleston Fire Department Fire Marshal Division, Information Bulletin IB-2019-11-06-03 Emergency Responder Radio Coverage (issued 11/14/2019, revised 05/26/2023)
erces_triggers.rule: Thresholds "offered to assist owners, developers and designers determine when to proceed with engineering evaluations": "Projects greater than 12,000 square feet in area per floor." "Projects that include 1 or more floors below grade level." "The project is greater than 3 floors above the lowest level of fire department access." erces_triggers.code: Charleston Fire Marshal Division Information Bulletin IB-2019-11-06-03 (rev. 05/26/2023)
erces_triggers.rule: "Construction permits shall be required for replacement of donor antennas, BDA, internal attenuators, or reprogramming of a BDA." "Maintenance shall be considered repair or replacement of system components that do not effect the inbound or outbound signal of the ERRC system. Examples will be system batteries, lighting arrestors, interior antennae."
erces_triggers.threshold: Any BDA, donor antenna or attenuator replacement or reprogramming.

erces_triggers.code: Florida Statutes 633.202(18) (2026 Florida Statutes)
erces_triggers.rule: "The local authority having jurisdiction shall determine the minimum radio signal strength for fire department communications in all new and existing buildings." (b): "all new and existing buildings must meet the minimum radio signal strength requirements for public safety agency communications as provided in the Florida Fire Prevention Code." (c)1: the AHJ may require "The installation of a two-way radio communication enhancement system in a new or existing building if the interior of the building does not meet the minimum radio signal strength". (i): AHJs "may not enforce requirements that are more stringent" than the FFPC and this subsection.
erces_triggers.threshold: New and existing buildings, minus the (h) exemptions. No local add-ons allowed.

erces_triggers.code: Florida Statutes 633.202(18)
erces_triggers.rule: Not required to meet minimum signal strength or have an assessment: "1. One- and two-family dwellings and townhouses. 2. Buildings having less than 12,000 total gross square feet with no underground areas. 3. Apartments and transient public lodging establishments that are less than three stories high and that have direct access from the apartment or guest area to an exterior means of egress. 4. Wood frame apartment buildings" covered by (a): "apartment buildings 75 feet or less in height that are constructed using wood framing, provided that the building has less than 150 dwelling units and that all dwelling units discharge to the exterior or to a corridor that leads directly to an exit", shown by building permit documents identifying wood frame construction.
erces_triggers.threshold: Exempt: 1-2 family and townhouses; under 12,000 gross sq ft with no underground area; apartments/lodging under 3 stories with exterior egress; wood-frame apartments 75 ft or less with under 150 units.

erces_triggers.code: Florida Statutes 633.202(18)
erces_triggers.rule: The AHJ may require an assessment of interior coverage "not more frequently than once every 3 years for an existing high-rise building and an existing building having more than 12,000 total gross square feet and once every 5 years for all other existing buildings, unless: a. Such building undergoes Level III building alteration or rehabilitation as defined in the Florida Building Code; b. Such building undergoes reconstruction as determined by the Florida Fire Prevention Code; c. A public safety agency reports ... devices failed to function correctly inside a building due to poor signal coverage; or d. A building is determined to be an imminent life safety threat to first responders."
erces_triggers.threshold: Level III alteration (work area over 50% of building area, FBC-EB 604.1) or reconstruction lifts the 3-/5-year limit and allows an immediate assessment.

erces_triggers.code: Florida Statutes 633.202(18)
erces_triggers.rule: "Existing high-rise buildings ... are not required to comply with minimum radio strength ... until January 1, 2025. However, by January 1, 2024, an existing high-rise building that is not in compliance ... must apply for an appropriate permit for the required installation with the local government agency having jurisdiction and must demonstrate that the building will become compliant by January 1, 2025." Same dates for existing high-rise apartment buildings.
erces_triggers.threshold: Existing high-rise buildings (FBC definition); deadlines already passed, so non-compliant high-rises are now open violations.

erces_triggers.code: Florida Fire Prevention Code 9th Edition, NFPA 1 (2024) Florida amendments, Rule 69A-60.003, effective 12/31/2026
erces_triggers.rule: 11.10.2: "In all new and existing buildings, the local authority having jurisdiction shall determine the minimum radio signal strength for fire department communications in accordance with section 633.202(18), F.S., and this Code. In all new and existing buildings, an approved emergency communication enhancement system shall be installed where the minimum radio signal strength into the building cannot be maintained in accordance with NFPA 1225." 11.10.2.1: "Where existing coverage at the exterior of the building does not meet or exceed delivered audio quality of 3.4 or greater for analog or digital systems, two-way radio communication enhancement systems shall not be required."
erces_triggers.threshold: From 12/31/2026: new and existing buildings that fail NFPA 1225 inside, unless outdoor DAQ is below 3.4; 633.202(18)(h) exemptions still apply.

erces_triggers.code: 2023 Florida Building Code, Existing Building, 8th Edition (2021 IEBC amended), ICC copy
erces_triggers.rule: Defines the Level III trigger used by 633.202(18)(c)2.a: "Level 3 alterations apply where the work area exceeds 50 percent of the building area." Level 2 (603.1) is the addition or elimination of doors or windows, reconfiguration or extension of any system, or added equipment where the work area is 50 percent or less. Change of occupancy (605) goes to Chapter 10; additions (606.2) to Chapter 11.
erces_triggers.threshold: Alteration permits whose work area is more than 50% of the building area.

trigger_notes: Strongest permit-data triggers found: Houston 1103.2.1 (every alteration to an existing building with a basement, more than 3 stories or more than 50,000 sq ft needs an ERCC compliance test before final or CO), Phoenix 2024 510.1.1 (retest on any tenant improvement or change of occupancy/use), SF AB 2.01 (a change-of-occupancy building permit triggers a coverage test), and Denver 510.1.2 (an MNS install or a full fire alarm head-end replacement in an existing high-rise, underground, I or E occupancy, or airport building triggers a test). Each of these maps to a permit type a feed can filter on: alteration/remodel/TI, change of occupancy, or fire alarm permit.

CO / final ties found in code or official text: NYC BC 901.5 (no occupancy until fire protection systems are tested; FDNY waivers for existing buildings need a final C of O), Seattle 510.5.4 items 11-12 (records and acceptance report before the CO), Houston 510.1.1 and 1103.2.1 (report before final approval or CO), Phoenix policy (Certificate of Radio Coverage Compliance before the CO; TCO case by case), LA County V7-C3-S21 (system off until final inspection), SF AB 2.01 (test on completion, recorded on the fire alarm or test permit).

No AHJ in this set uses a percentage-of-area alteration threshold in the text read. The only area thresholds are building-size gates: NYC 250,000 sq ft; Seattle 50,000 sq ft total or 10,000 sq ft basement; Denver 50,000 / 100,000 / 12,000 / 10,000 gsf by construction type and occupancy; Phoenix and Houston 50,000 sq ft; LA County 10,000 sq ft; SF 12,000 sq ft one-story exemption. Seattle's 'substantial alteration' (SDCI Tip 314: 7,000 sq ft floor, 2-year look-back) is not tied to ERCES in the 2021 SFC.

Los Angeles City: no LAFD alteration threshold was found. The LA Fire Code text read (2023 edition, UpCodes) is the model CFC 510 and 1103.2 with no LA change. The only LA-specific thresholds (more than 3 stories, 50,000 sq ft, 10,000 sq ft basement, 2 levels below grade) come from a 2022 BOMA trade article. LAFC on codes.iccsafe.org and LAMC 57.510 on amlegal returned 403. LA moved to the 2025 CFC cycle on Jan 1, 2026 per the state schedule; the 2026 LA amendments were not checked.

Chicago is the outlier: its building code does not adopt IBC 918 radio coverage and relies on wired two-way firefighter phones in high-rises. Treat Chicago permits as a weak ERCES signal unless the Chicago Fire Prevention Code (not found online, not checked) or a CFD policy adds a requirement.

NYC section numbers moved: 2014 BC 403.4.4 / 907.2.13.2 / 917 and FC 511 / 3 RCNY 511-01 became 2022 BC 916 (916.3 where required), FC 510 and 3 RCNY 510-01. In the 2022 code, BC 403.4.4 is the emergency voice/alarm section. NYC permit data: BC 916.3 means any NB (new building) job over 75 ft (BC high-rise) or over 250,000 sq ft gross needs ARCS unless the FDNY bulletin exemption applies (R-1/R-2/B, roof 150 ft or less, 1 story below grade or less, 250,000 sq ft or less).

Edition status as read: NYC 2022 code (LL 77/2023); SF 2025 SFFC; LA 2023 LAFC on UpCodes; Chicago 2019 BC; Seattle 2021 SFC; Denver 2025 DFC (2024 IFC); Phoenix 2024 PFC (effective Feb 17, 2026 per UpCodes); Austin 2024 IFC (effective July 10, 2025); Houston 2021 HFC.
SF AB 2.01 (2025) carries a DRAFT watermark in the PDF text layer, so the Addendum G wording may still change.

Third-party copies marked verified false: LA County V7-C3-S21 (hosted by Safer Buildings Coalition; the county site was not reached) and Houston CE-1350 (hosted by a vendor; houstonpermittingcenter.org returned 403). UpCodes copies of adopted codes were treated as verified.

Best permit-data signals in this set: Montgomery County MD (new building with any below-grade floor, any floor over 25,000 sq ft, total over 100,000 sq ft, or over 3 stories; certified test before the occupancy permit); Florida 633.202(18)(c)2.a (a Level III alteration, work area over 50% of building area, lets the AHJ order an immediate coverage assessment of an existing building of 12,000 sq ft or more); Virginia VEBC 801.1/803.1 (every addition is new construction, so VCC 918 applies to it); DC 1103.2 (any existing building with no working radio or wired system, timing set by OUC); DC OUC retest rule (adding walls, ceilings or partitions in a building with a system means a retest by an OUC-approved vendor, which maps to tenant fit-out permits).

Retest after additions or remodels: model IFC 510.6.1 (2018, 2021, 2024), DC 510.6.1, NC 510.6.1, SC 510.6.1 and MN Appendix P P106.1 all use "structural changes ... including additions or remodels that could materially change the original field performance tests". None gives a percentage, area or dollar threshold. Virginia deletes 510.6 entirely, so there is no code retest trigger there.

Existing-building retrofit (1103.2) is gone in Virginia (SFPC Chapter 11 deleted in its entirety) and North Carolina (NC Fire Code 510.2 Deleted; Chapter 11 DELETED). In both states an existing building gets ERCES only through new work (additions, VA locality request under SFPC 510.2) or voluntary install.

Change of occupancy: Virginia VEBC 704.1 limits change-of-occupancy fire protection to sprinklers (704.2), fire alarm (704.3) and standpipes (704.4), so a change of occupancy alone does not trigger VCC 918 there. Maryland is the opposite: COMAR 29.06.01.05B(4)(c) makes a change of occupancy classification a 'new building or condition'. No ERCES provision was found in VEBC Chapter 6 (alterations).

Fire alarm replacement as a trigger: only through the model 1103.2 wording 'where an existing wired communication system cannot be repaired or is being replaced' (IFC 2018/2021/2024, SC 2024, MN Appendix P, DC 1103.2). That is the wired firefighter phone system, not the fire alarm panel in general. Fairfax requires a fire alarm permit for any full ERCES (supervision), which links the two permit types in its records.

Building-size exemptions found: model IFC 2024 and SC 2024: one-story 12,000 sq ft or less, no below-ground area; NC's code in force (2018): one-story 7,500 sq ft or less, not windowless, underground or with a basement; Virginia VCC 918.1 Exc. 3: above-grade single-story under 20,000 sq ft, and Exc. 2: Type IV or V without basement and not unlimited area; Florida 633.202(18)(h): under 12,000 total gross sq ft with no underground area; DC: R-2 with 4 or fewer units per floor up to 3 floors, R-3, IRC buildings; Montgomery: only below-grade floors, over 25,000 sq ft per floor, over 100,000 sq ft total or over 3 stories are covered at all.

Virginia: the locality, not the owner, runs the acceptance test (VCC 918.1.1) and installs and operates any extra radio equipment (918.1.1, 918.1.2); the owner installs cabling and space. VCC 918.1 Exception 6 exempts buildings in localities that do not provide the equipment, so the trigger depends on the locality's program. Fairfax notes that VCC 'imposes limitations on requirements for ERCES' and that high-rise firefighter phones are still required unless a code modification lets ERCES replace them.

Arlington County: beyond Ch. 8.1 510.2.1, the fee table cites 'Zoning-Site Condition # 37', which suggests a standard site plan condition requires in-building radio in site plan projects; the condition text itself was not found. The FY2026 DPSCEM budget states the department will 'Manage the County's in-building wireless program to ensure newly constructed buildings comply with communication standards for first responders' (https://www.arlingtonva.us/files/sharedassets/public/v/2/budget/documents/fy-2026/fy-2026-proposed/gf-21-dpscem-fy26p.pdf). The 2023 Fire Protection Requirement Manual (2018 code edition) only lists 'emergency responders radio coverage' as a fire command center and standby power item.

DC is still on the 2017 DC Construction Codes (12-H DC Fire Code effective May 29, 2020, per UpCodes adoption info). DOB's code modernization release says the first set of proposed rules is due mid-to-late fall 2026 and final rules in winter 2027 (https://dob.dc.gov/release/dc-department-buildings-advances-modernization-district-construction-codes). The OUC process document says DC has mandated public safety radio coverage for newly constructed buildings since January 2015.

Maryland: NFPA 1 2024 base text (11.10) could not be read on NFPA's site (paywalled; UpCodes Maryland NFPA 1 2024 chapter 11 returns no section text). The Florida amendment document shows NFPA 1 2024 numbering 11.10.2. COMAR amends NFPA 1 9.15.1/9.15.2 (inserting 'and the AHJ' after 'NFPA 1225') and makes no 11.10 amendment. Montgomery County amends NFPA 101 9.15 (ERRCES) and NFPA 1 11.10.11.1 (test procedure 'unless otherwise directed by the AHJ').

Prince George's County: no ERCES-specific county rule found. DPIE's Fire & Life Safety Section page does not list BDA/ERRCS among third-party-review systems. A search excerpt said DPIE enforces the 2021 IBC and 2021 NFPA 1/101 from March 1, 2026 (not read on the DPIE page). The county site returned 403 to scripted fetches.

Minnesota: IFC 510 is deleted statewide (7511.0510) and ERCES exists only where a local ordinance adopts Appendix P. Bloomington adopts it (§ 6.02(a)(2)). Minneapolis § 173.380 adopts the MSFC and § 173.420 lists its amendments; neither mentions Appendix P, so Minneapolis has not adopted it in the text read (Municode, read 2026-11-04). Shakopee City Code 130.07 adopts IFC Appendices B, C, D, E, F and G only and says Appendix H is not adopted; Appendix P is not adopted. No Scott County ordinance on radio coverage was found; county radio is ARMER. The 2024-IFC-based MN fire code is in rulemaking (Request for Comments Feb 2, 2026; effective date TBD); the Fire Code TAG (Sept 11, 2025 notes) accepted FCCP 4 so that 2024 IFC 510 design and performance rules apply 'when a jurisdiction voluntarily adopts requirements for these systems' (https://www.dli.mn.gov/sites/default/files/pdf/TAG-fire-code-091125-notes.pdf). No 'Appendix Q' text was found.

North Carolina, corrected 11/5: the state lists the 2018 codes as currently effective, so 7,500 sq ft is the figure in force. The ICC copy of the 2024 NC Fire Prevention Code shows Exception 4 at 12,000 sq ft one-story; UpCodes and the NCOSFM 2018-code amendment file show the older 7,500 sq ft wording. The NCOSFM hearing notice (https://www.ncosfm.gov/240610-notice1hearing-2/open) records the petition 'granted' with a proposed effective date of January 1, 2025. Treat 12,000 sq ft as current, pending the Rules Review Commission record (not checked). SL 2025-50 exemptions apply now by statute (Sec. 1.(e)); Building Code Council rule text adopting them was not checked.

Jacksonville NC, Onslow County, Wilmington: no local ERCES text in the chapters read 2026-11-05. Jacksonville 8-63 adopts the most recent NC Fire Prevention Code and 8-63.1 its appendix, changing only Appendix D. Onslow 6.5-4 adopts Volume V of the NC State Building Code, naming the 1991 edition, with later amendments taking effect by themselves. Wilmington 3-16 applies the NC Fire Prevention Code. A search excerpt of an Onslow County fire marshal job posting (not read) says county fire inspections in unincorporated areas are done by the Planning and Development Department. NC state law applies (2018 NC Fire Code 510 plus SL 2025-50).

South Carolina: the state adopts IFC with Building Codes Council modifications; no state modification to IFC 510 or Chapter 11 appears in the 2024 index (https://llr.sc.gov/bcc/PDFfiles/2024%20Final%20Modification%20Index%20with%20Hyperlinks.pdf). 2024 SC Fire Code implementation date is January 1, 2027 (https://llr.sc.gov/bcc/PDFfiles/2024%20Code%20Adoption%20Notice.pdf). No Columbia or Greenville ERCES amendment or bulletin was found; Charleston's bulletin is guidance on the state code, not a local amendment.

Florida: 633.202(18)(i) bars local AHJs from enforcing anything more stringent than the FFPC and the statute on requirement, design or installation of an enhancement system, so Florida counties and cities should match the state triggers. The 9th Edition FFPC (NFPA 1 2024) takes effect 12/31/2026; the 8th Edition (NFPA 1 2021) is in force on 2026-11-04.

NFPA 1225 (2022) Chapter 18 and 20.3.10.1 (Georgia OCI copy, https://oci.georgia.gov/document/document/nfpa-1225-chapter-18/download, a state agency posting, not NFPA): 18.5 requires testing per 20.3.10 and 20.3.10.1; 20.3.10.1.1 'All new systems shall be initially acceptance tested'; 18.7.3 allows an AHJ renewable permit. No alteration or remodel retest rule was found in the chapter 18 text read, so NFPA 1225 adds no alteration trigger beyond what the adopting fire code says.
